text: SPOTREP 0231/Apr. At 2218Z patrol boat Wren, on station near Saltholm Sound, sighted a fishing trawler, MV Aldous Bay, drifting with engines stopped about 4 nautical miles west of Saltholm light. The trawler is Danish-flagged and showed no navigation lights. Three persons were seen on deck. The trawler did not answer VHF calls on channel 16 over ten minutes. Wren held position at 1 nautical mile and photographed the vessel. The crew assesses possible engine failure or a radio problem; low confidence.

SPOTREP 0232/Apr. At 2250Z patrol boat Wren sighted a tanker, MV Orsa Bright, steaming east at 13 knots about 7 nautical miles north of Saltholm light. The tanker is Norwegian-flagged and displayed full navigation lights. It answered a VHF call on channel 16 within one minute and gave its destination as Brevik. Eleven persons were seen on the bridge wings through the night scope. Wren photographed the vessel at 2 nautical miles. Assessment: routine transit, high confidence.

TRACKREP B-17. Radar Hollin held track 2208 from 0310Z to 0344Z, a four-engine jet transport at 33,000 feet heading 095 degrees at 470 knots groundspeed. It squawked 1126 and was on a filed flight plan from Kasra to Venn. The track left coverage to the east at 0344Z and was handed off to Venn centre. Operator rating: routine.

TRACKREP B-18. Radar Hollin held track 2215 from 0322Z to 0331Z, a small helicopter at 900 feet heading 180 degrees at 80 knots groundspeed. It squawked no code and filed no flight plan. It hovered for two minutes near the Brack quarry at 0327Z before continuing south. The track was lost at 0331Z in low-level clutter. Operator rating: unknown, request follow-up.

PATROL SUMMARY 8-02. A foot patrol at observation post Ash saw four tracked vehicles and two wheeled armoured vehicles parked in a tree line 1.5 kilometres north of Elm village at 0530 local. Engines were off. Camouflage netting covered three of the vehicles. About twenty personnel were seen cooking and checking equipment. The patrol sketched the layout. Assessment: probable company-size halt, medium confidence. The patrol withdrew at 0610 after a dog alerted near the position.

PATROL SUMMARY 8-03. A foot patrol at observation post Birchfield saw a farm tractor pulling a trailer of hay bales along the track south of Moss village at 0600 local. Two civilians walked alongside. No military equipment or markings were seen. The patrol watched for 25 minutes and took no photographs. Assessment: agricultural activity, high confidence. The patrol remained in position.

EMITTER NOTE 9-11. Site Larch recorded a continuous-wave carrier on 156.80 MHz at 1840Z, bearing 200 degrees. The carrier was frequency-modulated with voice and lasted 6 minutes. Signal strength was moderate. The frequency is the marine distress and calling channel, and the voice was in an unidentified language. Site Larch alone had coverage, so no fix was obtained. The recording was passed to the language team.

EMITTER NOTE 9-12. Site Moor recorded a frequency-hopping signal in the 225 to 400 MHz band at 1915Z, bearing 090 degrees. It hopped about 100 times per second and lasted 22 minutes. Signal strength was strong. The hopping pattern matched a known military radio family in the library. Sites Moor and Nye both obtained bearings, giving a fix about 25 kilometres east of Moor. A report was sent to the duty officer.

IMAGERY NOTE 10-04. Satellite pass of 20 April over Port Velis, resolution 0.3 metres, cloud cover 5 percent. Compared with the 6 April pass, three cranes were operating at the container quay, up from one. Fourteen ships were alongside or at anchor, up from nine. A new storage yard of roughly 120 containers had appeared south of the quay. The analyst assesses increased port throughput, medium confidence.

IMAGERY NOTE 10-05. Satellite pass of 20 April over Port Harrow, resolution 0.3 metres, cloud cover 40 percent. Compared with the 6 April pass, one crane was operating at the main quay, unchanged. Six ships were alongside or at anchor, down from eight. A dredger was working in the approach channel. The analyst assesses no significant change in throughput, medium confidence; cloud limited the view of the western berths.

SENSOR LOG 11-07. Seismic sensor array Quarry-North was offline from 0900Z to 1300Z on 3 May for scheduled firmware upgrade. Version 4.2 replaced version 3.9. One technician performed the upgrade remotely. Detection threshold was lowered from 12 to 10 units. Neighbouring array Quarry-East provided partial coverage during the outage. The array passed its self-test at 1300Z.

SENSOR LOG 11-08. Acoustic sensor Harbour-3 was offline from 2200Z on 5 May to 0630Z on 6 May after a fault in its hydrophone cable. Two divers replaced the cable section. The sensor's detection range is unchanged at about 5 kilometres. No other sensor covered the harbour mouth during the outage. The sensor passed its self-test at 0630Z.
